steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Snores)

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Scratches ear)

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Medjehtiqedti!

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: As if it wasn't enough that you went off by yourself first thing in the morning, now you're slamming doors and disturbing my nap! Have you repaired the harp, or have you been enjoying Athenius so much you forgot about your job?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: There's no use trying to repair the harp...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Giving up so soon? You can't fix a tiny crack like that? What were you doing in all those classes you took in Columbia?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Just filling in the crack and painting over it isn't hard. But it's not just the harp that was damaged—

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: It was also your fragile bleeding heart?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It was also Sargon's reputation.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Kereseira's harp was one of the best-preserved relics I've ever seen.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Wooden instruments are highly sensitive. The slightest blemish on the body could change its sound.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: That was why we were very careful during the appraisal process and avoided any destructive tests...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: I've heard it a million times at the museum—

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: 'The ornaments, string materials and lacquer are typical of the Minoan style. Historical records indicate that it very likely belonged to Kereseira herself.'

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But something didn't feel right when I was repairing it last night...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The wood chips that fell from the crack indicate that the material was mountain firs, the kind that ancient Minoans often used, but something was off with the cross-section texture.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: The weapons of the heroes are made from ancient trees. They'll have some pretty deep texture.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: No, it didn't look like the natural texture of wood. It was reminiscent of a certain moisture retention technique developed in Sargon.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I read about it in old books about instrument-making. Minoan plants are rich in moisture, while the climate in Sargon is generally dry.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Wood imported from Minos had to be specially treated to prevent them from cracking due to the dryness.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The cross-section I saw showed signs of such treatment.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You mean this was not Kereseira's original harp, but a replica made by Sargonians using Minoan wood? You sure you're not overthinking it?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I didn't want to believe it, but I just took the wood chips to a lab.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Testing revealed the presence of Sargonian resin, dating back about a hundred years...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Oof...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The harp looked perfect. It was virtually impossible to tell that it was a replica without destructive testing. I doubt Padishah Khery knew anything.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I have to tell the Astynomos. We can't give the Minoans a fake harp under the eyes of Kereseira's statue!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The exchange ceremony must be stopped!
Ambassador Medjehtiqedti's mission was to 'carry out' the exchange ceremony.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Behnui Effendi...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: We made an oath to the padishah before we set out. How can you continue to call yourself the ambassador of Sargon, if you fail to retrieve the engineering data from the construction of the Three Poleis?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes, I have my duties as ambassador. As an archaeologist, however, I can't overlook such a mistake, much less intentionally participate in a lie.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: That's why I say you have no political acumen. You see yourself as a museum curator, not a diplomatic envoy.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: The important thing about the relic exchange ceremony is not the relic, but the exchange. Who cares if the harp is a replica? It still makes a sound.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You want to offer up a fake harp at the ceremony?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Absolutely not!

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: And what is your bright idea, Medjehtiqedti, without the authentic harp and a ceremony right around the corner?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: In the halls of Menat-Ha'mait, you told Padishah Khery that you loved the legends of Minos, and wanted to see true heroism with your own eyes.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Is your idea of heroism clinging to your obsessions and bringing shame to your country at the very first cultural exchange between Sargon and Minos since the establishment of diplomatic relations?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Are you and your useless father one and the same?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: He ruined your family, turned the name Nasutu Mashayer into a high society joke.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: In his obsession with literature, he abandoned his duties, even his duty to his daughter, forcing her to chase the shadows of heroes in books, failing to find any heroism in her father.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This has nothing to do with him! I only love Minoan stories because—

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: 'As emissaries of Sargon, our priority is to carry out the exchange ceremony successfully—not our own obsessions and interests.'

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Your words, verbatim.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'll find a way, before the ceremony, no matter what it takes. I can't let a fake...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Obstinate fool.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Very well. You can meditate while I act on your behalf and carry out the duty that the Sargonian ambassador was supposed to perform.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: It not as if it changes anything. To the Astynomos and the guests, you're nothing more than a curious girl, an enthusiastic volunteer for the temple project while I negotiated with the Astynomos—

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I am, for all due intents and purposes, the true ambassador of Sargon.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Hello. Maybe you don't remember me, but I've visited this ranch quite a lot lately. The herder, Melitta, knows me.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Please, stop leaning on the fence and let me through.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Opens sleepy eyes)

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: It was not my intention to interrupt your nap. Perhaps you will enjoy this grass. The dew is still fresh on it.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I also brought some berries.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Well, I'm out of bribes. In that case...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Would you like a dream interpretation? Kýrios... maybe kýria.

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Brushes teeth on the fence)
Cauliflower is a girl. Berries are too sweet for her, and grass isn't filling enough. You need carrots to draw her attention.
If you find a burdenbeast has a fever and not even its favorite food can coax it to move...
Just scoop some water with a leaf and spray it on its horn to cool it down!

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You really know your burdenbeasts, Melitta. I didn't know there were so many tricks to getting a burdenbeast to move.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: Of course. They're not like beckbeasts, which are used to taking commands. A herder needs a hundred tricks to coax burdenbeasts into doing what you need them to.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: It's this understanding that builds a bond between burdenbeast and herder.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: Am I right, Cauliflower?

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Sways tail)

steps.name: Burdenbeast
steps.text: (Gets up and leaves)

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: Maybe it's a talent, to know one more way to get burdenbeasts to move than other herders.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Thanks for getting Cauliflower to move, Melitta.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: No problem.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: The priestess of Endymion Temple gracing us with her presence means that this place is blessed by the heroes. We couldn't be happier.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: As long as it doesn't cause any trouble for you.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: Of course not! All you do is admire the sights and look at the fence.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: A little while back, I was concerned that a foal could slip through the cracks in the fences. A few days later, you filled the gaps with strong threads.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Just doing my part.

steps.name: Melitta
steps.text: It was a very kind deed. I won't disturb you anymore; I have a few hooves to trim.
Kassandra leans towards the 'filled fence', where delicate threads stand in regular intervals, gleaming in the sun.
She plucks one of the threads, hearing nothing except the breeze blow over the pasture.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Of course it wouldn't make a sound. Not even a burdenbeast running into it did...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: There isn't much time. When will you sing again?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I know what you're here for, Kýrios Behnui.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Rest assured that the relationship between our two nations is the highest priority. A little incident will not be allowed to affect it.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: A little incident?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Xanthos came to Athenius five years ago, working as ferryman and manager of the crossing. He took in an apprentice, Lykeion, a former priest school student.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: They are accused of attempting to steal from the room of Ambassador Medjehtiqedti. They are being held in custody, pending trial in accordance with the law.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Since the ambassador has elected not to press charges—

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: A justification to comfort the ignorant people by a naive girl moonlighting as supervisor of the rebuilding of the First Temple, not the decision of the honored ambassador of Sargon.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I see your views differ from Kyría Mashayer's.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I will, of course, take full responsibility for this matter as Astynomos. However, I would ask that the two of you come to an agreement as to how we deal with it.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You know what I mean, Astynomos. My view is that of the Sargonian delegation.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: This tragedy, the theft and destruction of the harp, would never have happened if the exchange ceremony was not repeatedly delayed.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I have reason to suspect that you have intentions other than promoting the relationship between our two nations, that you have intentionally delayed the ceremony, and everything that took place did so on your orders.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I hear the position of Astynomos was newly created following the administrative reform of Athenius, and you were rewarded with the role because of your contributions to said reforms.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: If something goes wrong with the first cultural exchange between our two nations since the establishment of diplomatic relations...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Then I congratulate you on being the only Astynomos who the people of Athenius will never forget.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: The exchange ceremony is certainly my most important task. I admit I was negligent for not arriving at the scene promptly due to a busy schedule.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: In that case, how would you define this incident... this 'theft and destruction of the harp'?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: The brutal, barbaric, ignorant, baseless hatred of the perpetrators... the robbery and destruction of this symbol of friendship between Sargon and Minos was a most despicable act.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: In my thirty years overseeing culture in Menat-Ha'mait, Sargon has received many letters from Minos requesting the return of the cultural artifacts that were removed during the occupation.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Shouldn't these plunderers of Minos's national treasure be severely punished, if you Minoans truly value it so much?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: They will be tried according to Minoan law. As far as the punishment is concerned, though...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I have no intention of leaving the impression that Sargon is trying to bully the people of Athenius. We are emissaries of peace, after all.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: This is a most sensitive time, however. Just because Sargon and Minos signed a truce five years ago doesn't mean that all is peaceful and well.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: The padishahs are used to solving problems with force of arms. I would not give them a reason to get angry, if I were you.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Xanthos and Lykeion conspired to steal and deface a national treasure and sabotage the exchange ceremony...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Their actions are tantamount to treason.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: They will be put on death row immediately.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Thank you, Astynomos. I look forward to the exchange ceremony in a few days.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Get in.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: What's going on? It's not normal to transfer prisoners so suddenly, before we're officially sentenced.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: I'm just following orders. Move quietly and behave yourselves... maybe there'll be a chance for clemency.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You really believed the Sargonian ambassador would protect the Minoans who tried to steal the harp.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: We heard what she said to the officer. It would have been easiest to make the accusations while everyone was watching. But she didn't do it.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You can never tell what someone is thinking. Submit an official assessment of the damage, put pressure on the Astynomos and peace officers... there are many things that the Sargonian delegate can do.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Death row, eh? We're getting the royal treatment.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You should regret it, Lykeion. Destroying a hotel kitchen is nothing compared to the charges we now face.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: All the more reason we had to take what's ours back from the bandits. The harp of Kereseira sings only for the stories of heroes. It will not, and must not, sing for a false peace.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: I know your past, Master Xanthos. I may not have experienced war for myself, but I respect your decision. I couldn't let you risk everything by yourself, having known about your plan.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: You saved my life two years ago.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It was your classmate from priest school, Hekádemos, who carried you down from the archery range after you were injured by an Originium shard.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I just took in a former student who wasn't willing to continue in the priesthood, that's all.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: An Infected can never become a priest. It's divine work, communing with the heroes and guiding the way for the people. I couldn't do it.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: As for Hekádemos, all he wants is someone to debate him...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Do not fool yourself, Lykeion. It will only make the pain worse, when you finally have to face it.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Master Xanthos?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: My friend brought technology from the nomadic cities when he came to my homeland after receiving divine revelation. He built a village in the barren swamps with us.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The people in the village respected him a lot, but he always had a dark look on his face, late at night.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I lied to myself and tried to convince him that the river in his dreams wasn't red with blood; it was red because of iron that the river brought from upstream, and that the revelation was supposed to bring him to us.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: But he didn't believe it...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: He was prepared to go to war from the beginning. I was fooling myself.

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: River... hah... young people these days are foolish enough to fight the Sargonians to the death because of a dream like that?

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: And the two of you are here because you stole things from the Sargonians?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The harp of Kereseira belongs to the Minoans.

steps.name: Hoarse Voice
steps.text: Even less worth it...

steps.name: Beggar?
steps.text: What truly belongs to the Minoans these days, after the Sargonians invaded a hundred years ago?
